Robotic automation in pharmaceutical compound screening

Abstract
We describe a robotic platform for high-throughput pharmaceutical compound screening with on-line UV/Vis readout.

Introduction
Modern compound libraries contain millions of candidates; robotic screening is required for tractable evaluation.

Methods
We deploy a six-arm robotic platform with high-throughput screening (10000 compounds per day) and integrated UV/Vis spectroscopy. Compound selection is rule-based; no Bayesian optimization or active learning is used.

Results
The platform screened 2.5 million pharma compounds over 240 days with a hit rate of 0.4%.

Discussion
While the throughput is substantial, the screening protocol is open-loop and does not adapt based on intermediate results.

Acknowledgements
Funded by Sanofi Research and the Riken pharma initiative. No external academic collaborators contributed to this work.

References
1. Hertzberg, R.; Pope, A. High-throughput screening: new technology for the 21st century. Curr Opin Chem Biol 2000.
